lessons.title: The Premier League ladder
lessons.objective: You can explain how Premier League places decide Europe and relegation.

payload.prompt: How many Premier League teams qualify for the Champions League?

options.text: Top 2
Top 4
Top 6

explanation.correct: Right. The top four Premier League teams qualify for the Champions League group stage, though sometimes a fifth place team can also qualify if England earns an extra place.
explanation.incorrect: England typically has four Champions League spots for the Premier League, though this can vary based on UEFA coefficients.
explanation.sayThisLine: Top four gets Champions League if England earns the extra place.

payload.template: The Premier League has {{teams}} teams and {{relegated}} are relegated each season.

explanation.correct: Correct. Twenty teams compete, and the bottom three go down to the Championship.
explanation.incorrect: The Premier League has 20 clubs, and three teams are relegated to the Championship each season.

payload.prompt: Who won the 2025-26 Premier League title?

options.text: Arsenal
Manchester City
Liverpool

explanation.correct: Arsenal won the title with 85 points, ending a long wait for the {{team}} faithful.
explanation.incorrect: Arsenal took the 2025-26 title with 85 points after a strong campaign.
explanation.sayThisLine: Arsenal finally got it, 85 points, that's champions.

statement.speaker: Jamie
statement.text: We need top four for Champions League football.

payload.question: What does Jamie mean?

options.text: His team has to finish in the top four places to play in Europe's biggest club competition
His team has already qualified
The team needs to win four matches to qualify
Finishing fourth automatically wins a trophy

payload.translation: A top-four finish in the Premier League earns entry into the Champions League, the most prestigious European club competition.

followUps.line: Is your team close to top four this season?
followUps.why: Continues the conversation about their team's position.

followUps.line: Have they played in the Champions League before?
followUps.why: Opens a question about their club's history.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If uncertain, ask which European competition their team is in this season.

payload.prompt: When can a 5th place team qualify for the Champions League?

options.text: Never, only top four qualify
When England earns an extra European place based on coefficient ranking
If the top four teams refuse to play

explanation.correct: Right. England's number of Champions League places depends on how English clubs perform in Europe. A strong season can earn a fifth qualifying spot.
explanation.incorrect: England's European qualification places are determined by UEFA coefficients. A good year for English clubs in Europe can earn a fifth Champions League spot.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fifth might get in if England earns the extra place.

lessons.title: FA Cup and the pyramid
lessons.objective: You can explain the FA Cup and the English pyramid.

payload.prompt: What makes the FA Cup special compared to the league?

options.text: It pays more money
Non-league and lower-division teams can face Premier League giants in the early rounds
It's played only in summer

explanation.correct: Exactly. The FA Cup is a knockout competition that starts with hundreds of teams from the lower divisions and non-league, creating the possibility of giant-killing moments.
explanation.incorrect: The magic of the FA Cup is that it draws teams from all levels of the English pyramid, so a fifth-tier team could theoretically face a Premier League side.
explanation.sayThisLine: It's the cup, so anything can happen.

statement.speaker: Sarah
statement.text: The cup magic could happen this weekend.

payload.question: What is she talking about?

options.text: An unlikely upset where a smaller team beats a much bigger one
A magical trick will occur during the match
The weekend is guaranteed to be fun
Her team will definitely win

payload.translation: In cup competitions, especially the FA Cup, smaller teams can produce unexpected upsets that feel like magic because they overcome much bigger opponents.

followUps.line: Has your team had a memorable FA Cup run?
followUps.why: Asks about their personal experience with the cup.

followUps.line: What's the biggest upset you can remember?
followUps.why: Invites them to share a famous cup moment.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You don't need to know every cup story, just that upsets happen and fans love them.

payload.prompt: Can a non-league team from the fifth tier or lower enter the FA Cup?

options.text: No, only Premier League and Championship teams
Yes, teams from all levels of the English pyramid can enter
Only teams from the top three divisions

explanation.correct: Yes. The FA Cup is open to hundreds of teams across all divisions of the English football pyramid, from the Premier League down to non-league.
explanation.incorrect: One of the unique features of the FA Cup is that it draws from the entire English pyramid, making giant-killings possible.
explanation.sayThisLine: The cup is open to everyone, that's why upsets happen.

payload.prompt: How many major competitions do Premier League teams typically compete in?

options.text: One (just the league)
Two (league and FA Cup)
Three or more (league, cups and European competitions)

explanation.correct: Right. Premier League teams play in the league, the FA Cup, the League Cup, and if they qualify, European competitions like the Champions League.
explanation.incorrect: A successful Premier League team in Europe can play in four or five competitions across a season: the league, two domestic cups, and European competition.
explanation.sayThisLine: They're playing three games a week, that's the full fixture list.

payload.prompt: Match the cup competition to its description.

pairs.definition: England's historic knockout cup, open to teams across all levels of the pyramid, where smaller teams can face giants.
A domestic knockout competition for the top divisions, often used by big clubs to rotate their squads.
The possibility of an upset where an unexpected team progresses far in a cup run.

explanation.summary: England has multiple domestic cups, but the FA Cup is the most historic and open to the widest range of teams.
explanation.sayThisLine: The FA Cup is where the real upsets happen.

lessons.title: Spending rules and the 2026/27 laws
lessons.objective: You can explain the spending rules and the new law changes fans are discussing.

payload.prompt: What is the Premier League's main spending rule designed to do?

options.text: Ensure every team spends the same amount
Limit spending and prevent clubs from going into serious debt (Profit and Sustainability Rules)
Give bigger clubs more money to spend

explanation.correct: Right. The Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR) limit how much clubs can spend relative to their revenue, to prevent financial collapse and promote competitive balance.
explanation.incorrect: The Premier League's spending rules restrict how much clubs can lose over three years. Teams that break these rules face points deductions.
explanation.sayThisLine: They got a points deduction for breaking the spending rules.

payload.prompt: Under the new 2026/27 rules, can VAR review a wrongly awarded corner?

options.text: No, VAR cannot review corner decisions
Yes, if it can be corrected quickly without lengthy review
Yes, always, no matter how long it takes

explanation.correct: Correct. Starting in 2026/27, VAR can review corners if the decision is clearly wrong and the review can be done quickly.
explanation.incorrect: A new 2026/27 rule allows VAR to review corner decisions, but only if the correction is immediate, not delaying the game.
explanation.sayThisLine: They can review a corner now, but only if it's quick.

statement.speaker: commentator
statement.text: They're stalling but the ref's got the countdown up now.

payload.question: What does this mean?

options.text: The team is deliberately wasting time and the referee is enforcing the new five-second restart countdown
The referee is timing the entire match
The match is ending soon
A goal will be scored in five seconds

payload.translation: The 2026/27 restart countdown forces teams to restart play (throw-in, goal kick) within five seconds, shown visually by the referee, cutting down on deliberate time-wasting.

followUps.line: Does your team need to improve at restarting quickly?
followUps.why: Asks if it affects their play style.

followUps.line: Do you think the countdown makes the game better?
followUps.why: Opens their opinion on the rule change.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you're unsure, note that the ref's hand signals count down the five seconds.

facts.label: Losses over 3 years
facts.value: £45 million (can only lose £40 million total under PSR)

options.text: Buy the striker for £60 million anyway
options.consequence: You exceed the spending limits and risk a points deduction that could actually hurt your league position more than the striker helps.
options.considerations: PSR violations are serious; the Premier League has deducted points from multiple clubs for breaches.

options.text: Spend your full £50 million on a striker and focus on sustainable budget
options.consequence: You strengthen the squad within financial rules, showing stability to investors and avoiding the risk of points deduction.
options.considerations: Building within constraints is how successful clubs manage their future; PSR is designed to prevent this exact overspending.

options.text: Wait and reduce losses before making big signings
options.consequence: You miss out on this target but move closer to sustainable spending and avoid any rules breach.
options.considerations: A conservative approach but safe; sometimes the best business is the business you don't do.

payload.expertNote: Experienced Premier League managers weigh immediate success against long-term sustainability. The PSR rules mean a points deduction today can undo signings from tomorrow.
payload.safetyNote: This scenario explains the rules; it is not financial or investment advice.

payload.prompt: Why did the Premier League introduce spending rules?

options.text: To make matches more exciting
To prevent clubs going bankrupt and to promote competitive balance
To guarantee teams stay in the league forever

explanation.correct: Right. Spending rules protect clubs from financial ruin and create fairer competition by preventing unlimited spending by the richest owners.
explanation.incorrect: The rules aim to maintain the financial health of clubs and stop a small number of rich owners from dominating through spending alone.
explanation.sayThisLine: Spending rules keep the league competitive and the clubs stable.
